passage: I've sat next to Devika for three years, so I noticed when she stopped celebrating. She got the senior analyst title in March, the one she'd wanted since college, and by April she was staring at the ceiling fan during lunch. One evening she said, "Manjula, I got everything on my list. Why do I feel like nothing?" I honestly didn't know what to say. Maybe she's just tired, or maybe it's bigger. Then she started staying back on Thursdays to teach two interns spreadsheets, and she came in looking lighter. She also phoned her old school teacher. I can't say what's going on in her head, but she seems to be looking for something other than titles.

qa.q: What title did Devika get in March?
qa.a: She got the senior analyst title in March.

qa.q: What was Devika wondering when she asked why she felt like nothing?
qa.a: She was wondering what it was all for, since she had ticked off everything on her list and still felt empty.

qa.q: What small commitments could help Devika find meaning?
qa.a: Keeping up things like teaching the interns and staying in touch with her old school teacher, small ongoing commitments to people and craft.

qa.q: How sure can Manjula be about Devika's inner state?
qa.a: Not sure at all. Manjula says it might be tiredness or something bigger, and only reports what was seen, such as the teaching and the phone call.

grounding: After reaching early goals Devika asks what it was all for; a coworker observes her turning toward teaching and relationships rather than status.
